item.title: Airbnb or Monthly Rentals: Which Suits Your Medellín Apartment? (2026)
item.description: Airbnb, furnished monthly rental or a yearly lease? Compare rules, work and income for your Medellín apartment, with a table and an owner checklist.
item.content:encoded:
Short answer: if your building and zone allow tourist rentals and you (or your manager) can look after guests every day, Airbnb can earn more per night, in exchange for more work and more requirements. If not, or if you want less turnover, a furnished monthly rental (stays of one to six months) is the middle option: the apartment stays furnished and you keep some flexibility, but you deal with one tenant at a time and no cleaning every other day. A traditional one-year lease is still the most stable, lowest-effort choice.

Our post Airbnb vs long-term rental in Medellín compares the two extremes. This guide is about the middle ground, which many owners overlook.

General information as of November 2026. This is not legal or tax advice: we are not lawyers or tax advisors, so please consult a qualified professional about your situation.

What is a monthly rental, exactly?

It means renting your apartment furnished and fully equipped to one person or family for one or several months: professionals on relocation, remote workers, families who have just arrived and are looking for a permanent home, or Colombians back for a season. Each stay is longer than a tourist booking and shorter than a standard lease.

The difference from short-term rental isn't only price. It's length of stay, and length changes the rules (as of November 2026):

  • Tourist housing (vivienda turística): Decree 1836 of 2021 (in Spanish), from Colombia's Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism, defines it as a home used for tourist accommodation for less than 30 days. It requires the National Tourism Registry (RNT) and, according to the Medellín mayor's office, express permission in the building's bylaws (reglamento de propiedad horizontal) and land use that allows it.
  • Urban housing lease: governed by Law 820 of 2003 (in Spanish). Article 5 says the term is whatever the parties agree and, if they don't set one, it is one year.

One practical catch: official summaries don't always use exactly the decree's wording ("less than 30 days"), so a stay of exactly 30 days can be a grey area. Before you set up a monthly contract, ask a lawyer and read your building's bylaws, which may have their own rules on how units are used.

Another one: as of November 2026, on Airbnb a "monthly stay" starts at 28 nights, and those bookings automatically get the long-term cancellation policy (Airbnb Help Center). So a 28- or 29-night booking is "monthly" to the platform but still under the decree's 30 days.

Airbnb vs monthly vs traditional lease: comparison table

FactorShort-term (Airbnb)Furnished monthly rentalTraditional lease
Typical lengthNights or weeks1 to 6 months12 months or more
Main frameworkTourist housing: RNT, bylaws and land useLease contract (ask a lawyer how to structure it)Law 820 of 2003
FurnishedYes, fully equipped for guestsYes, for living: kitchen, desk, internetFurnished or unfurnished
OperationsDaily: messages, check-ins, cleaning between staysMedium: one tenant, move-in and move-out, final cleanLight: rent collection, inspections, repairs
TurnoverHighLowVery low
IncomeVaries with season and occupancySteadier for the length of each stayFixed; yearly increase capped at CPI (Art. 20)
Main riskSanctions if you operate without the requirements; low-season monthsEmpty weeks between tenantsLate payment and empty months between leases
Your own useBlock dates whenever you likeBetween staysOnly when the lease ends

When does a monthly rental make sense?

Tick the ones that apply:

  • Your building's bylaws do not authorize tourist rentals, or the owners' assembly is discussing restricting them.
  • Your address is in a zone where land use limits tourist accommodation (the 2026 revision of Medellín's land-use plan, the POT, concentrates it in mixed-use zones; the mayor's office sums it up in Vivienda turística y POT: dónde sí, dónde no, in Spanish).
  • The apartment is already furnished and you don't want to sell or remove the furniture.
  • You want less wear and tear, less noise for neighbors and fewer cleanings than with Airbnb.
  • You want to use the apartment a few weeks a year, which is hard with a 12-month lease.
  • You live outside Medellín and would rather deal with one tenant at a time.

If you ticked three or more, it's worth running the numbers on monthly rentals before you decide.

Which earns more?

It depends on your building, neighborhood, unit size and season, and there is no official figure comparing the three models in Medellín. Be wary of citywide averages: run the exercise with your apartment's numbers.

  • Short-term: nightly rate × booked nights per year, minus platform fees, cleaning, utilities, internet, supplies, building fee, management fee and taxes.
  • Monthly: monthly rent × occupied months (count the empty weeks between tenants), minus utilities and internet if included, move-out cleaning, building fee, management fee and taxes.
  • Traditional: monthly rent × 12, minus empty months between leases, maintenance, management fee and taxes. For 2026, the maximum increase at renewal is 2025 inflation, which DANE put at 5.10% (Noticias RCN).

Always compare net, not gross, and count the time you or your manager will spend on each. For the full calculation, see how to calculate your Medellín rental yield. For taxes on that income, talk to an accountant.

What to check before renting by the month

  1. Your building's bylaws. See what they say about how units are used, move-ins, visitor registration and pets.
  2. A written contract with move-in and move-out dates, the rent, what's included (utilities, internet, cleaning) and the notice period.
  3. Guarantee. Law 820 does not allow cash deposits in urban housing leases (Art. 16); ask a lawyer which guarantees you can request given how your contract is set up.
  4. A photo inventory at move-in and move-out.
  5. Utilities in whose name. If they're included in the rent, put a reasonable cap in writing.
  6. Building fee paid up. The owner remains liable for it even when the unit is rented; we explain why in apartment management in Medellín.

How Medellín Concierge can help

We provide property management in Medellín for both short-term and longer rentals:

  • Short-term: listings on Airbnb, Booking.com, Expedia and VRBO, dynamic pricing, 24/7 guest support, cleaning and maintenance, and RNT, SIRE and TRA registrations. More on Airbnb management in Medellín.
  • Longer rentals: for owners living in Colombia or abroad. More on property management in Colombia. On our monthly rentals in Medellín page you can see how we present furnished apartments to people looking for a place to live for a few months.
  • Both: an owner portal and monthly GAAP financial statements.

Our fees are published on our plans. For the bigger picture, read our Medellín property management guide.

Not sure which model suits you? Request a free consultation and we'll look at your building, your zone and your numbers together.

FAQ

Do I need an RNT to rent my apartment by the month?

The RNT is required for tourist housing, which Decree 1836 of 2021 defines as accommodation for less than 30 days. A lease of several months is generally governed by Law 820 of 2003. Because there are nuances (stays of exactly 30 days, for example), ask a lawyer about your contract (information as of November 2026).

Can I rent by the month if my building doesn't allow Airbnb?

The express bylaw authorization the mayor's office requires refers to tourist housing. A monthly housing lease is a different arrangement, but read the full bylaws: they may have rules on how units are used. If in doubt, ask the building's administration and a lawyer.

Which earns more: Airbnb or monthly rentals?

There's no general answer and no official figure for Medellín. It depends on occupancy, rates, costs and the management time each model takes. Compare net yearly income using your own apartment's numbers; we're happy to do that exercise with you in a free consultation.

item.title: How Much Does It Cost to Rent an Apartment in Medellín in 2026?
item.description: What renting an apartment in Medellín costs in 2026: sourced rent data, furnished vs unfurnished costs, the 5.10% increase cap and a budget checklist.
item.content:encoded:
Short answer: The cost to rent an apartment in Medellín in 2026 depends mostly on three things: the neighborhood, whether it is furnished, and how long you stay. Public figures point to a rising market. Medellín's real estate observatory (OIME) put rents for apartments in El Poblado at COP 53,812 per square metre per month in July 2026, and the portal Ciencuadras put the average Medellín listing at about COP 4.9 million a month (El Colombiano, El Colombiano). Our own furnished monthly rentals start from COP 6.9 million per month as of November 2026 (monthly rentals page).

This guide is for travellers, remote workers and anyone planning a move to Medellín. It is general information as of November 2026, not legal or financial advice.

What does rent in Medellín cost in 2026? The numbers we can source

There is no single official "average rent" for Medellín. Different sources measure different things, so here they are side by side, with what each one actually measures:

SourceFigureWhat it measuresDate
OIME, Alcaldía de Medellín (via El Colombiano)COP 53,812 per m² per month (COP 15,851 in 2014)Rent per square metre for apartments in Comuna 14 (El Poblado)July 2026
Ciencuadras (via El Colombiano)About COP 4.9 million per month (national average about COP 3.7 million)Average asking rent on one listing portal2026
DANE (via Noticias RCN)5.10%2025 consumer price inflation, the legal cap for 2026 rent increases on renewalPublished January 2026
Fedelonjas (via El Colombiano)Building fees up 17.14% a yearNational change in cuotas de administración (building fees)2026
Medellín Concierge (monthly rentals page)From COP 6.9 million per monthOur own furnished monthly apartmentsNovember 2026

To turn the OIME figure into a monthly rent: a 90 m² apartment in El Poblado at COP 53,812 per m² works out to about COP 4.8 million a month, unfurnished and before utilities. That is a rough illustration from one data point, not a quote.

Why do the numbers vary so much?

You'll find guides online quoting very different figures for the same city. The usual reasons:

  • Asking price vs agreed price. Portal averages show what landlords ask, not what tenants end up paying.
  • Furnished vs unfurnished. Most public data is about unfurnished long-term leases. A furnished monthly apartment bundles furniture, equipment and often services, so it costs more on paper.
  • Neighborhood and estrato. El Poblado, Laureles and parts of Envigado sit at the top of the market. In Colombia, utilities are also billed by the property's socio-economic stratum (estrato), and, as of November 2026, homes in estratos 5 and 6 pay a contribution on top of the cost of the service (Ley 142 de 1994, art. 89).
  • Sample and date. A portal average changes with whatever is listed that week.

If you're choosing between areas, our comparison of El Poblado vs Laureles vs Envigado for a month and our guide to El Poblado apartments for rent cover the trade-offs.

Unfurnished lease or furnished monthly rental: what will I actually pay?

The headline rent is only part of the bill. Use this checklist to compare like with like:

CostUnfurnished long-term leaseFurnished monthly rental
RentMonthly canon, usually on a 12-month contractOne monthly price, for stays of one month or more
Building fee (administración)Ask whether it is included; listings often show it separatelyAsk whether it is included
Utilities (water, power, gas)Usually paid by you, billed by estratoAsk: included, capped or extra
InternetYou set up and pay the contractAsk for the speed and whether it is included
Furniture and kitchenYou buy or bring themIncluded
GuaranteeOften a fiador (co-signer) or rental insurance policy; as of November 2026, cash deposits are not allowed in urban housing leases under Ley 820 de 2003, art. 16Set by the contract; get the deposit and refund terms in writing
CleaningYour ownAsk how often, if at all

Building fees deserve a close look in 2026: Fedelonjas reported they rose far faster than rents (El Colombiano), so a "rent only" price can hide a growing extra.

A furnished monthly rental usually costs more than the bare rent of an unfurnished lease, but you skip the furniture, the utility contracts and, in many cases, the fiador. For a stay of a few months, the total is often the fairer comparison. See how to rent a furnished apartment in Medellín without a fiador for how that works.

How much can rent go up in 2026?

For urban housing leases under Ley 820 de 2003, the landlord can raise the rent once every 12 months of the contract, by no more than the previous year's consumer price inflation (Ley 820 de 2003, art. 20). DANE put 2025 inflation at 5.10%, so as of November 2026 that is the cap for increases applied during 2026 (Noticias RCN). The increase is not automatic; it applies on the contract's anniversary.

Short furnished stays for tourists work differently: as of November 2026, apartments offered as vivienda turística must be registered in the National Tourism Registry, RNT (MinCIT), and the price is simply what your booking says. Which rules apply depends on how the contract is set up, so ask, and consult a qualified lawyer if anything is unclear.

How to budget for a Medellín apartment: a 5-step checklist

  1. Decide your length of stay. Under three months, compare furnished monthly prices; for a year or more, an unfurnished lease may be cheaper.
  2. Pick two or three neighborhoods, then compare prices within them, not across the city.
  3. Ask for the full monthly total in pesos: rent, building fee, utilities, internet and cleaning.
  4. Check the guarantee: fiador, insurance policy or deposit, and when you get it back.
  5. Get everything in writing before paying, and pay by a traceable method. If you're a foreign guest, bring your passport: as of November 2026, accommodation providers report foreign guests to Migración Colombia through SIRE (Migración Colombia).

Working remotely? Our guide to working remotely from Medellín adds internet and coworking costs to the picture.

Then email us your dates, budget and number of guests at sales@medellinconcierge.net. Prefer to chat? Use the WhatsApp button on our rentals page. We'll tell you what is available and exactly what the price includes.

Own an apartment in Medellín? Read our Medellín property management guide, or see how our Airbnb management in Medellín and property management in Colombia work for owners at home and abroad. Medellín Concierge offers property management in Medellín; request a free consultation.

FAQ

What is the average rent in Medellín in 2026?

There is no single official average. The portal Ciencuadras put the average Medellín listing at about COP 4.9 million a month in 2026, and the city's OIME put El Poblado apartment rents at COP 53,812 per m² per month in July 2026. Ciencuadras measures asking prices on its portal; the OIME figure comes from a sample of properties the observatory visited, not an official rent index.

How much is a furnished apartment in Medellín per month?

It depends on the neighborhood, the building and what's included. Our own furnished monthly rentals start from COP 6.9 million per month as of November 2026; email us your dates for an exact quote.

How much can my landlord raise the rent in 2026?

For urban housing leases under Ley 820, up to the previous year's inflation, applied on the contract's anniversary. With DANE's 2025 figure of 5.10%, that is the cap for 2026 increases as of November 2026.

item.title: Apartment Management in Medellín: What a Manager Does and What It Costs (2026)
item.description: Building fee or rental manager? What apartment management in Medellín covers, what managers charge (+ IVA), costs owners keep and a pre-signing checklist.
item.content:encoded:
Short answer: in Medellín, "administración" can mean two very different things. One is the building fee (cuota de administración), which you pay to your building or complex (the propiedad horizontal, roughly an HOA) for common areas, security and upkeep. The other is rental management of your own apartment: a company that finds and looks after tenants or guests, collects rent, maintains the unit and reports to you, usually for a percentage of rental income plus VAT. They are different contracts, costs and people.

This guide explains what each one does, what it costs and what to check before you sign. For the big picture, start with our Medellín property management guide.

General information as of November 2026. This is not legal or tax advice: we are not tax advisors or lawyers, so please consult a qualified professional about your situation.

What is the building fee, and who charges it?

If your apartment is in a building or gated complex under Colombia's horizontal property regime, Law 675 of 2001 (in Spanish) sets the rules. Under that law:

  • The building's administrator is appointed by the owners' assembly or, where one exists, by the board (consejo de administración) (Article 50).
  • That administrator has powers of execution, upkeep, representation and collection for the building (Article 51). In other words, they work for the building as a whole, not for you as an individual owner.
  • Every owner must contribute to common expenses, even if they don't live in the unit, and for ordinary expenses the owner and the occupant are jointly liable (Article 29).

That last point matters if you rent out: even if the lease says the tenant pays the fee, the building can also collect it from you. Someone should check every month that it is paid.

No outside company sets the fee. Each building's assembly approves it with the yearly budget, so it varies a lot from one building to the next.

What does a rental apartment manager do?

This is the company or person you hire so your apartment earns income without you being there. Depending on the rental model, the work usually looks like this:

TaskLong-term rentalShort-term rental (Airbnb and similar)
Finding occupantsAdvertising, showings and tenant screeningListings on Airbnb, Booking.com, Expedia and VRBO
PricingMonthly rent and the yearly legal increaseDynamic nightly and seasonal pricing
CommunicationWith one tenantWith every guest, before and during the stay
RegistrationsThe leaseRNT, SIRE reporting and TRA
CleaningAt move-in and move-outBetween every stay
MaintenanceRepairs owed by the landlordRepairs and restocking supplies
Payments and reportsCollecting rent and paying the ownerSettling bookings and costs, paying the owner

For short stays, the apartment also needs a National Tourism Registry (RNT) number, which according to MinCIT (as of November 2026) is renewed every year between January 1 and March 31, and your building's rules must allow tourist use. We cover that in Airbnb requirements in Medellín.

How much does an apartment manager in Medellín charge?

There is no official rate. The usual model is a percentage: of the monthly rent for long-term rentals, or of booking income for short-term rentals. VAT (IVA) is added to that commission when the company is registered for it; Colombia's general rate is 19% under Article 468 of the Tax Statute.

Before comparing quotes, ask what amount the percentage is calculated on (gross, after the platform's commission, or after costs), what it includes and what is billed separately. In how much Airbnb management costs in Medellín we show with an example how that base changes your real cost.

Our published fees

Medellín Concierge publishes its fees. As of November 2026:

PlanLong-termShort-term
Basic12% + IVA17% + IVA
Premium15% + IVA20% + IVA

The Premium plan also includes paying the property tax (predial), the building fee, utilities and internet on the owner's behalf. The details of each plan are on our property management fees page.

Which costs stay with the owner?

Even with a manager, the apartment's own costs are still yours (on the Premium plan we pay them for you out of rental income, but they don't go away):

  • The building fee (cuota de administración).
  • Property tax (see property tax in Medellín).
  • Utilities and internet, if the tenant doesn't pay them.
  • Repairs and maintenance.
  • For short-term rentals, each platform's commission and guest supplies.
  • Taxes on your rental income, which depend on your situation: ask an accountant.

How can you tell whether a rental agency is registered?

Law 820 of 2003 (Article 28, in Spanish) requires anyone in the business of renting out other people's property to hold a landlord registration (matrícula de arrendador). Decree 51 of 2004 says they must register in every municipality where they operate and show the registration number in their advertising. In Medellín the registration is handled by the Alcaldía; see the official matrícula de arrendadores page. If a company won't show you its number, ask why.

Checklist before you sign with a manager

  • What is the percentage, what is it calculated on, and does it include IVA?
  • Which services are included, and which are extra (cleaning, repairs, supplies)?
  • Does the company hold a landlord registration, if it manages long-term leases?
  • For short-term rentals: who keeps the RNT, SIRE and TRA up to date?
  • Who checks that the building fee and property tax are paid?
  • How often are you paid, and to which account (including one abroad)?
  • What report do you get each month, and can you see bookings or payments online?
  • How long is the contract, and how do you end it?

How we help

We offer property management in Medellín for both models. For short stays, our Airbnb management in Medellín covers listings on Airbnb, Booking.com, Expedia and VRBO, dynamic pricing, 24/7 guest support, cleaning and maintenance, and RNT, SIRE and TRA compliance management. For stays of 30 nights or more, see our long-term property management in Medellín; if you own from abroad, see property management in Colombia. Either way, you follow everything in the owner portal, with monthly GAAP financial statements.

Want to know which model suits your apartment and what it would cost? Request a free consultation and we'll go through it with you.

FAQ

Does the owner or the tenant pay the building fee in Medellín?
A lease can pass it to the tenant, but under Article 29 of Law 675 of 2001 the owner and the occupant are jointly liable for ordinary common expenses, so the building can collect it from you. Check every month that it is paid.

How much does an apartment manager charge in Medellín?
There is no official rate; it is usually a percentage of the rent or of bookings, plus IVA where it applies. Our plans, as of November 2026, run from 12% + IVA (long-term Basic) to 20% + IVA (short-term Premium); see our plans and the fees page.

Can my building's administrator rent out my apartment?
That is a different role. The building administrator works for the building as a whole (Article 51 of Law 675). To rent out your apartment you need your own manager or agency, with a contract signed with you.

Last reviewed: November 2026. General information, not legal or tax advice. Rules change: confirm with the official source or a qualified professional. Our current fees are always on the fees page.

item.title: El Poblado Apartments for Rent: Furnished Monthly Options and What's Included (2026)
item.description: Renting a furnished apartment in El Poblado, Medellín? Which part to choose, what monthly prices include, and how to book safely. Updated November 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Short answer: El Poblado is the easiest part of Medellín to rent a furnished apartment by the month: it has the widest choice of furnished units, walkable cafés and coworking, and two Metro stations along its western edge. Before you book, check three things: which part of El Poblado the apartment is in (the area is large and hilly), exactly what the monthly price includes, and whether the contract fits your stay. Our own monthly furnished rentals start from COP 6.9 million per month (as of November 2026, see our monthly rentals page); email us your dates for a quote.

This guide is for travellers, remote workers and people testing Medellín before a longer move. It is general information as of November 2026, not legal advice.

Where exactly is El Poblado?

El Poblado is Comuna 14 of Medellín, one of the city's 16 urban comunas according to the Alcaldía de Medellín. It is not one neighborhood but a whole district made up of many barrios, including Manila, Astorga, Castropol, Lalinde, La Florida, Los Balsos, El Tesoro, Las Lomas and La Aguacatala. Names you'll see in listings, such as "Provenza" or "Parque Lleras", are popular areas rather than official barrios.

That matters when you rent, because "El Poblado" on a listing can mean a flat street five minutes from the Metro or a hillside building where you'll take a taxi for every errand.

Which part of El Poblado should I rent in?

A simple way to think about it:

  • Lower Poblado, near the river and Avenida Las Vegas (for example around La Aguacatala, Manila and Astorga): flatter streets and the closest access to Metro Line A, which stops at Poblado and Aguacatala stations (Metro de Medellín).
  • Central Poblado, around Parque Lleras and Provenza: the most restaurants, bars and cafés within walking distance, and also the most noise on weekend nights.
  • Upper Poblado (barrios such as Los Balsos, Las Lomas, El Tesoro and Altos del Poblado): quieter, greener and more residential, but steep, so most people rely on taxis or ride apps.

If you're still deciding between areas of the city, our comparison of El Poblado vs Laureles vs Envigado for a month covers the trade-offs.

How much does a furnished apartment in El Poblado cost per month?

There is no official average rent for furnished monthly apartments in El Poblado. Listing portals and booking sites show asking prices that change daily and mix furnished and unfurnished units, so treat them as a snapshot, not a market rate.

What drives the price in El Poblado is the same as elsewhere, only more pronounced: the exact barrio, the building's amenities, the size of the unit and the season. For our own apartments, the published figure is from COP 6.9 million per month as of November 2026; the exact price depends on the apartment, your dates and the length of stay, so email us for a quote. For a wider view of the city, see our guide to furnished apartments for rent in Medellín.

One local detail: in Colombia, utilities are billed by the property's socio-economic stratum (estrato), and homes in estratos 5 and 6 pay a contribution on top of the cost of the service that helps subsidise lower estratos (Ley 142 de 1994, art. 89, explained by the Constitutional Court, C-086 de 1998). Much of El Poblado's housing is in estratos 5 and 6, so ask which estrato an apartment is in. That's one reason an "all-in" monthly price can be better value than a lower rent plus bills.

What is included in a furnished monthly rental?

Ask for the inclusions in writing. This is the checklist we suggest for any El Poblado apartment:

ItemWhat to askWhy it matters in El Poblado
Utilities (water, power, gas)Included, capped or paid by you?Estrato 5 and 6 rates make utilities a real line in your budget
InternetSpeed, and is there a backup?Essential if you work remotely; ask for a recent speed test
Building fee (administración)Included in the rent?El Poblado buildings with pools, gyms and 24-hour reception have higher fees
CleaningHow often, and is linen changed?Weekly cleaning is common in furnished rentals but never guaranteed
DepositAmount, and when is it returned?Get the refund conditions in the contract
ParkingIncluded or extra?Useful in upper Poblado, where you may rent a car
NoiseWhich side of the building, how close to Lleras or Provenza?Weekend nightlife carries further than you'd expect

For remote workers, our guide to working remotely from Medellín goes deeper into internet, desks and backup power.

How do I book an El Poblado apartment safely?

  1. Send your dates, budget and number of guests. It's the fastest way to get a real answer on availability.
  2. Confirm the exact barrio and building, not just "El Poblado".
  3. Get the price and the inclusions in writing, in pesos.
  4. See the apartment in person or on a live video call. Anyone can request a property's certificado de tradición y libertad from the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro to check the registered owner.
  5. Read the contract before paying. For tourist stays, as of November 2026, apartments offered as vivienda turística must be registered in the National Tourism Registry (RNT) (MinCIT), so you can ask for the RNT number. Residential leases follow Ley 820 de 2003. Which applies depends on how the contract is set up; consult a qualified lawyer if anything is unclear.
  6. Bring your passport. Accommodation providers report foreign guests to Migración Colombia through the SIRE system (Migración Colombia).
  7. Pay by a traceable method and photograph the inventory at check-in.

No Colombian co-signer? See how to rent a furnished apartment in Medellín without a fiador.

Ready to stay in El Poblado? Email us

Browse our furnished rentals in El Poblado, all our furnished rentals in Medellín and our monthly rentals page, then email us your dates, budget and number of guests at sales@medellinconcierge.net. Prefer to chat? Use the WhatsApp button on our rentals page. We'll tell you which apartments are available for your dates and exactly what the price includes.

Own an apartment in El Poblado? Read our Medellín property management guide, or see how our Airbnb management in Medellín and property management in Colombia for owners abroad work. Medellín Concierge offers property management in Medellín with dynamic pricing, 24/7 guest support, cleaning and RNT, SIRE and TRA compliance management; request a free consultation.

FAQ

Is El Poblado a good place to rent an apartment for a month?

For a first stay, yes for most people: it has the widest choice of furnished apartments and services within walking distance. If you want quiet nights or flat streets, choose lower or upper Poblado carefully, or compare Laureles and Envigado.

How much is a furnished apartment in El Poblado per month?

There is no official average; it depends on the barrio, building and what's included. Our own monthly furnished rentals start from COP 6.9 million per month as of November 2026. Email us your dates for an exact quote.

Are utilities included in El Poblado monthly rentals?

It depends on the apartment, so always ask. Many El Poblado homes are estrato 5 or 6, where utilities cost more, which makes an all-inclusive price worth comparing.

item.title: How to Rent Out Your Medellín Apartment While Living Abroad: Power of Attorney, Contract and Payments (2026)
item.description: Living abroad? How to rent out your Medellín apartment: power of attorney at a consulate or with an apostille, remote lease signing and getting paid.
item.content:encoded:
Short answer: yes, you can rent out an apartment in Medellín without being in Colombia. Usually someone in the city acts for you under a power of attorney (poder) signed abroad, either at a Colombian consulate or before a local notary with an apostille; the lease is signed remotely or by your attorney-in-fact or manager; and the rent reaches you by bank transfer with a monthly income and expense report.

This guide walks through those three steps: who signs for you, what a manager can do while you are away, and how you get paid. It is general information as of November 2026, not legal or tax advice. Consular procedures and rules change, so confirm current requirements with your consulate and a qualified lawyer in Colombia before you sign anything.

For the full picture of registrations (RNT, TRA, SIRE) and taxes for overseas owners, start with our guide to managing a Colombian property from abroad. This article focuses on the practical side: signatures, contracts and payments.

Do I need a power of attorney to rent out my apartment from abroad?

Not always, but it almost always helps. There are two ways to work:

  1. You sign everything remotely. You e-sign the lease and your management agreement, and the manager runs day-to-day operations under that agreement.
  2. You give a power of attorney to someone you trust or to your manager. The attorney-in-fact can sign the acts the poder lists on your behalf: the lease, the handover, paperwork with the building administration or utility companies.

A poder matters most when a party asks for an in-person or authenticated signature, or when something needs signing quickly and you are in another time zone.

How do I sign a power of attorney outside Colombia?

Colombia's Foreign Ministry (Cancillería) has explained that a poder to be used in Colombia can be granted abroad before a Colombian consul or before the official that local law authorizes (Foreign Ministry Concept 16 of 2010; the national legal defense agency repeats the rule in its Circular 06 of 2023). In practice, you have two routes:

At a Colombian consulateBefore a notary where you live
How it worksSignature recognition on a private document (special poder) or a public deed (general poder)The local notary certifies your signature
Extra stepUsually none; confirm with the consulateApostille from the country where you signed (1961 Hague Convention), or legalization if that country is not a party
AppointmentUsually requiredDepends on the notary
Best forOwners near a consulateOwners far from a consulate

What the consulates themselves publish:

  • Bring the poder unsigned plus valid ID; you sign in front of the officer. See, for example, the signature-recognition guides of the Colombian Consulate in Frankfurt and the Consulate in Brussels. Both 2024 guides list a fee of EUR 18 per signature; fees vary and each consulate publishes its own, so check yours.
  • Special vs general poder. The Consulate in Toronto.pdf) handles a special poder through signature recognition and a general poder through a public deed, and warns that a general poder carries high risks. It also notes that the consulate does not review what your poder says; that is up to you and your lawyer.
  • The apostille comes from the country where you signed. The Cancillería only apostilles Colombian public documents that will be used abroad (Concept 16 of 2010). If you sign before a notary in the US or Spain, that country's competent authority issues the apostille.

Practical tip: for renting, a special poder with specific powers is usually more prudent than a general one. Have a lawyer in Colombia review the wording, and ask the notary or office where it will be used whether they accept it as drafted.

What a poder to rent your property should cover

A lawyer drafts it for your case, but it should make clear:

  • Your details and your attorney-in-fact's, plus the apartment's address and property registration number (matrícula inmobiliaria).
  • What the attorney-in-fact may do: sign the lease, receive and hand over the property, sign inventories, handle utilities.
  • What they may not do: sell, mortgage or collect money other than rent, if that is your wish.
  • How long the poder is valid.

Can I sign the lease remotely?

As of November 2026, Colombia's Law 527 of 1999 recognizes data messages and electronic signatures, and Decree 2364 of 2012 (now compiled in Decree 1074 of 2015) gives an electronic signature the same effect as a handwritten one if the method reliably identifies the signer. So use an e-signature platform that records identity, date and acceptance, not just a PDF emailed back and forth.

Long-term residential leases are governed by Law 820 of 2003, with its own rules on rent increases, guarantees and termination. Our guide to long-term rental management in Medellín covers them, including why cash deposits are not allowed on residential leases.

What can a manager do while I am not in Medellín?

With a clear management agreement (and a poder where needed), a manager in the city can handle almost everything:

  • Short-term rentals: list the property, adjust pricing, support guests 24/7, register every guest in SIRE and TRA, coordinate cleaning and maintenance. See our Airbnb management in Medellín.
  • Long-term rentals: show the property, screen the tenant, prepare the lease, hand over with an inventory and photos, collect rent and handle repairs. See our long-term property management in Medellín.
  • Both: pay the property bills you authorize and send you reports.

Keep for yourself, or for a specific poder: selling, mortgaging, changing the property's use or suing a tenant. For those, always use a lawyer.

How do I get paid?

Agree on this in writing from day one. A common setup:

  1. Rent or booking payouts go into an account identified for your property.
  2. Expenses you approved are deducted (management fee, cleaning, utilities, building fees, repairs).
  3. You receive the balance on a fixed date, to an account in Colombia or abroad, as agreed and as your bank allows.
  4. Each month you get a statement with receipts.

Two points for your accountant: registering your foreign investment with Banco de la República if you bought with money from abroad, and withholding tax and income tax filing for a non-resident in Colombia. We summarize both, with DIAN sources, in our guide for owners abroad. We are not tax advisors: consult a qualified Colombian accountant or tax lawyer. And don't forget property tax (impuesto predial), which stays your responsibility while you live abroad.

Checklist before renting from abroad

  • Decide: short-term or long-term rental
  • Check the building's bylaws (and RNT, if short-term)
  • Special poder signed at the consulate, or before a notary with an apostille, reviewed by a lawyer
  • Management agreement signed: services, fee, expenses, payout date
  • Lease ready for a reliable e-signature or your attorney-in-fact's signature
  • Account to receive funds and transfer method agreed
  • Photo inventory at handover
  • Colombian accountant for taxes and foreign exchange

See our property management in Colombia for owners abroad, read the complete Medellín property management guide and compare our plans and fees.

FAQ

Can I rent out my Medellín apartment if I live abroad?

Yes. You can sign remotely or give a power of attorney to someone you trust or to your manager to sign and hand over the property for you. For short-term rentals, the property also needs an RNT and building rules that allow it.

Where do I sign a power of attorney if I live outside Colombia?

At a Colombian consulate (by appointment) or before a notary where you live. In the second case, the document usually needs that country's apostille. Confirm requirements with your consulate and a lawyer in Colombia, as of November 2026.

Is an electronically signed lease valid in Colombia?

Law 527 of 1999 and Decree 2364 of 2012 recognize electronic signatures when the method reliably identifies the signer. Use a platform that records identity and acceptance, and consult a lawyer if in doubt.

item.title: Furnished Apartments for Rent in Medellín: Prices, Neighborhoods and How to Book (2026)
item.description: Furnished apartments for rent in Medellín by the month: what drives the price, El Poblado vs Laureles vs Envigado, and how to book safely.
item.content:encoded:
Short answer: A furnished apartment in Medellín rented by the month is the simplest way to stay a few weeks or months without a Colombian co-signer or a one-year lease. The price depends mainly on the neighborhood, the size of the unit and what the rent includes; at Medellín Concierge, our monthly furnished rentals start from COP 6.9 million per month (as of November 2026, see our monthly rentals page). To book, send the owner or manager your dates, budget and number of guests, confirm what is included in writing, and pay only after you have verified the apartment and signed a contract.

This guide explains what drives the price, which neighborhoods renters usually compare, and the exact steps to book safely. It is general information as of November 2026, not legal advice.

How much does a furnished apartment in Medellín cost per month?

There is no official average price for furnished monthly rentals in Medellín. Listing portals such as Fincaraíz and Metrocuadrado show asking prices that change every day and mix furnished and unfurnished units, so treat any number you see there as a snapshot, not a market rate.

For our own apartments, the figure we publish is simple: monthly furnished rentals from COP 6.9 million per month, as of November 2026. The exact price for your stay depends on the apartment, the dates and the length of stay, so email us for a quote.

Prices in Colombia are quoted in pesos. If you are budgeting in dollars or euros, use the day's official exchange rate (TRM), which is certified by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia, and remember that your bank or card will apply its own rate and fees.

What makes one furnished rental cost more than another?

When you compare two apartments, the monthly number only tells half the story. These are the factors that usually explain the difference:

FactorWhat to askWhy it matters
NeighborhoodWhich barrio, and how far from where you'll spend your days?Location is the biggest price driver and shapes your daily routine
Size and layoutBedrooms, bathrooms, square metres, a real desk?A second bedroom or office changes both price and comfort
What's includedUtilities, internet, building fee (administración), cleaning?An "all-in" price can be cheaper than a lower rent plus bills
Length of stayIs there a different price for 1, 2 or 3+ months?Longer stays are often priced differently; ask, don't assume
Building amenitiesElevator, gym, pool, 24-hour reception, backup power?Amenities raise the price but may save you a gym or coworking fee
Season and datesDo your dates fall in high season or around holidays?Demand changes through the year, so book early for December and January

Which neighborhoods should I compare?

Most people looking for a furnished apartment for a month or more end up comparing three areas. We covered them in detail in El Poblado vs Laureles vs Envigado: where to stay in Medellín for a month; here is the short version:

  • El Poblado (Comuna 14 of Medellín, according to the Alcaldía de Medellín): the most restaurants, cafés, coworking spaces and services in English. Convenient for a first stay; busier and noisier near the nightlife streets.
  • Laureles (part of Comuna 11, Laureles-Estadio): flatter, more residential and with a local feel, still well connected to the rest of the city.
  • Envigado: a separate municipality just south of Medellín in the Valle de Aburrá metropolitan area, quieter and more family-oriented.

If you will work remotely, our guide to working remotely from Medellín explains what to check in the apartment itself: internet, desk, noise and backup power.

How do I book a furnished apartment in Medellín?

Here is the process we recommend, whoever you rent from:

  1. Send your dates, budget and number of guests. This is the fastest way to get a real answer about availability and price. Mention if you need parking, a pet-friendly building or a workspace.
  2. Ask what the price includes. Utilities, internet, the building fee, cleaning and any deposit or guarantee should be written down, not just mentioned on a call.
  3. Verify the apartment and the person renting it. See it in person or on a live video call. Anyone can request a property's certificado de tradición y libertad from the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro to check the registered owner.
  4. Read the contract before paying. It should state the dates, the monthly price, what is included, house rules and what happens if you leave early.
  5. Have your passport ready. As of November 2026, accommodation providers in Colombia report foreign guests to Migración Colombia through the SIRE system, and the reporting rules ask for a valid passport or another document authorised by Migración Colombia (Resolución 2357 de 2020, Migración Colombia).
  6. Pay by a traceable method and keep every receipt.
  7. Check in and document the inventory. Take photos of the furniture and condition on arrival, so the check-out is simple.

Short stay or monthly contract: does it matter?

It can. In Colombia, as of November 2026, apartments offered to tourists as vivienda turística must be registered in the National Tourism Registry (RNT), which is managed for the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism through the chambers of commerce (MinCIT, RNT portal). For short stays, it is reasonable to ask for the listing's RNT number.

As of November 2026, longer residential leases are governed by Ley 820 de 2003, which, among other things, limits cash deposits for urban housing leases (Article 16). Whether a specific furnished stay is a tourist stay or a residential lease depends on how the contract is set up, so read it carefully and consult a qualified lawyer if anything is unclear. If you don't have a Colombian co-signer, our guide on renting a furnished apartment without a fiador explains the usual alternatives.

Booking checklist

  • Dates, budget and number of guests sent
  • Monthly price confirmed in pesos, in writing
  • What's included listed: utilities, internet, building fee, cleaning
  • Apartment seen in person or on live video
  • Owner or manager identity checked
  • Written contract read before paying
  • Passport ready for check-in
  • Payment made by a traceable method, receipts saved

Ready to book? Email us

Browse our furnished rentals in Medellín and our monthly rentals page, then email us your dates, budget and number of guests at sales@medellinconcierge.net. Prefer to chat? Message us on WhatsApp from the button on our rentals page. We'll tell you which apartments are available for your dates and exactly what the price includes.

It depends on the neighborhood, size and what's included, and there is no official average. Our own monthly furnished rentals start from COP 6.9 million per month as of November 2026; email us your dates for an exact quote.

item.title: Property Tax in Medellín (Impuesto Predial): How It's Calculated, When It's Due and How to Pay From Abroad (2026)
item.description: How Medellín's impuesto predial is calculated, 2026 due dates and discount, and how foreign owners can pay property tax from abroad.
item.content:encoded:
Short answer: property tax in Medellín (the impuesto predial) is a yearly municipal tax that the owner pays, calculated on the property's cadastral value. In 2026 the city billed it in four quarterly installments and gave a 5% discount to owners who paid the whole year by March 27 and were up to date on earlier years. You can pay online, in the HaciendaMed app or at banks, including from abroad if you have an accepted payment method.

This guide is for owners, in Colombia or overseas, who want to understand their predial bill and avoid surprises. It is general information as of November 2026, not tax advice.

What is the predial, and who has to pay it?

The impuesto predial unificado is a tax each municipality charges on the real estate inside its borders. If your apartment is in El Poblado or Laureles, the District of Medellín bills you. If it is in Envigado or Sabaneta, that municipality bills you, with its own calendar and its own discounts.

The owner pays it, Colombian or foreign, living in Medellín or not. It doesn't matter whether the unit is empty, on a long-term lease or on Airbnb: the obligation stays with the owner. Don't confuse it with income tax on your rental income, which is filed with DIAN and depends on your tax residency.

How is property tax calculated in Medellín?

The basic formula is cadastral value (avalúo catastral) × rate (per thousand).

  • Cadastral value: the value Medellín's cadastre assigns to your property. It is usually different from the market price. The city explains how cadastral values are adjusted each year and when a full cadastral update happens.
  • Rate: set by Medellín's city council in the District's tax code. It depends on how the property is used (residential, commercial, vacant land) and, for homes, on the estrato and the value bracket. Your bill shows the rate applied.

How much can the predial go up from one year to the next?

When a city updates its cadastre, values can jump. To soften that, as of November 2026, Law 1995 of 2019 caps how much the tax itself can rise year on year: generally by inflation (IPC) only for estrato 1 and 2 homes valued up to 135 minimum wages, and by inflation plus eight points for other properties, with exceptions (for example a change of use or new construction). The cap applies to the tax, not to the cadastral value.

In 2026 Medellín kept rolling out its cadastral update comuna by comuna, applying those limits (Alcaldía de Medellín). If your comuna was updated, read your 2027 bill carefully when it arrives.

When is property tax due in Medellín?

ItemWhat happened in 2026Source
BillingFour quarterly installments, with dates by comuna2026 tax calendar
Annual payment discount5% for paying the full year by March 27, 2026Alcaldía de Medellín
Discount conditionBeing up to date on previous yearsPortafolio
Late paymentEach installment has a due date and a later date with a surcharge; after that, late interest applies2026 tax calendar

The city sets the predial calendar and any discount each year, so don't assume 2027 will match 2026. If it follows the 2026 pattern, the key decision comes in the first quarter: pay the full year with the discount, or pay by installment. Confirm the dates in the official calendar once it is out.

How do you pay Medellín property tax from abroad?

The city lists these payment channels:

  1. Online at medellin.gov.co/pagoimpuestos, through PSE or Place to Pay, with a debit or credit card.
  2. The HaciendaMed app, to check and pay from your phone.
  3. In person at authorized banks and bank correspondents.

Checklist for owners who live overseas

  • Keep your matrícula inmobiliaria (registration number) or código predial (CBML) handy. Both appear on your deed and your certificado de tradición y libertad.
  • Check that the email and mailing address on file with the city are yours, so the bill reaches you.
  • Decide how you will pay: PSE works with Colombian bank accounts. If you only have a foreign card, test Place to Pay well before the deadline, or put someone you trust in charge of the payment.
  • Put the first-quarter annual discount in your calendar.
  • Save every payment receipt, and if you plan to sell, request the paz y salvo (tax clearance) early.
  • Read each year's bill: if the cadastral value or the amount changes a lot, ask Medellín's cadastre office.

What happens if you don't pay?

Unpaid predial accrues late interest, and the city can start a collection process (cobro coactivo). If you plan to sell, you will usually need a predial paz y salvo, so confirm the requirements with your notary. Arrears also cost you the early-payment discount, which in 2026 was only for owners up to date. Property tax is one of the running costs to include when you work out your real rental yield in Medellín.

Can your property manager pay the predial for you?

Yes, it is a payment you can delegate. At Medellín Concierge, the Premium plan includes paying your property taxes (the predial), HOA fees (administración), utilities and internet for you, and you follow everything in your owner portal, with monthly GAAP financial statements. See the details in our plans.

If you are running a property from another country, also read managing a Colombian property from abroad and our complete guide to Medellín property management. Learn more about our property management in Medellín, Airbnb management in Medellín and property management in Colombia.

Want your predial, bills and rent off your to-do list? Request a free consultation.

FAQ

Do foreigners pay property tax in Medellín?
Yes. The predial is paid by the property owner, whatever their nationality or where they live. The rate and calculation are the same as for a Colombian owner.

When will Medellín announce the 2027 predial discount?
The city sets the calendar and any discount each year. In 2026 the discount was 5% for paying the full year by March 27, for owners up to date on earlier years. Check the city's tax calendar in early 2027.

Is property tax for Envigado or Sabaneta paid to Medellín?
No. Each municipality collects its own predial, with its own calendar and payment channels. If your property is in Envigado or Sabaneta, contact that municipality's treasury office (Secretaría de Hacienda).

Last reviewed: November 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice. We are not tax advisors: rates, dates and discounts change every year, so confirm with the Alcaldía de Medellín or a qualified professional.

item.title: Working Remotely From Medellín: Internet, Coworking, Time Zone and Where to Live (2026)
item.description: Working remotely from Medellín? Time zone, real internet speeds, coworking, public Wi-Fi, plugs, power-cut risk and a checklist for your monthly apartment.
item.content:encoded:
Short answer: Medellín works well for remote workers. Colombia stays on UTC-5 all year, so you overlap the whole US working day; fixed internet in the metro area is fast by Colombian standards; and the city has a public innovation hub, private coworking spaces and hundreds of free public Wi-Fi points. The things that make or break your month are specific to the apartment you pick: the real Wi-Fi speed, a proper desk, and a plan B if the power or connection drops.

This guide covers what to check before you book. For neighborhoods, read El Poblado vs Laureles vs Envigado: where to stay in Medellín for a month, and for how long you can legally stay, our Colombia digital nomad visa guide.

General information as of November 2026. Rules, prices and services change, so confirm details before you travel.

What time zone is Medellín in?

Colombia uses UTC-5 all year and does not use daylight saving time. The legal time was set by Decreto 2707 de 1982, and the Instituto Nacional de Metrología keeps and distributes Colombia's official time.

Because your home country may change its clocks while Colombia doesn't, the gap moves during the year:

Your team is inWhen your home country is on standard (winter) timeWhen your home country is on daylight saving (summer) time
New York / TorontoSame time as MedellínMedellín is 1 hour behind
Los Angeles / VancouverMedellín is 3 hours aheadMedellín is 2 hours ahead
LondonMedellín is 5 hours behindMedellín is 6 hours behind
Madrid / BerlinMedellín is 6 hours behindMedellín is 7 hours behind

For North American teams that means normal office hours. For European teams, expect early mornings: a 9:00 meeting in Madrid is 3:00 a.m. in Medellín in winter, so check your meeting schedule before you commit to a long stay.

Is the internet in Medellín good enough for video calls?

Generally yes, in a well-equipped apartment. In Ookla's Speedtest data for the second half of 2025, Envigado, the municipality just south of El Poblado, ranked among the fastest of Colombia's most populous cities for median fixed download speed, as reported by Finance Colombia.

A city median is not a promise for one apartment, though. Speed depends on the plan the owner pays for, whether the building has fiber, where the router sits and how many people share it. So:

  • Ask for a recent screenshot of a speed test taken inside the unit, showing both download and upload. Upload matters for video calls and file sharing.
  • Ask whether you can plug in a cable at the desk, which is usually more stable than Wi-Fi for long calls.
  • Keep a local SIM with a data plan as a hotspot backup.

Where can I work outside the apartment?

You have three kinds of options:

  1. Ruta N, Medellín's public innovation agency, runs a complex in the north of the city with coworking areas, offices and meeting rooms. See its workspaces page for current options and who they are for.
  2. Private coworking spaces, found in El Poblado, Laureles and other areas, usually sell day passes and monthly memberships. Prices and hours change, so check directly with each space.
  3. Free public Wi-Fi: as of mid-2026 the Alcaldía reported hundreds of public Wi-Fi points across the city, in places such as parks and public buildings. It's handy for email between errands; for client calls or anything confidential, use your apartment's connection or your phone's hotspot plus a VPN.

Will my laptop and chargers work?

Colombia uses Type A and Type B plugs (the same flat-pin plugs as the US and Canada) at about 110 to 120 V and 60 Hz, as Remitly's guide to electrical outlets in Colombia explains. Most laptop and phone chargers are rated 100 to 240 V, so visitors from Europe or the UK usually need only a plug adapter, not a voltage converter. Check the label on your charger.

What about power cuts in late 2026 and early 2027?

This one is worth knowing this season. Colombia relies heavily on hydropower, and with a strong El Niño forecast, the grid operator XM has warned of a risk of energy rationing, and EPM, Medellín's utility, raised its rationing-risk alert to orange, naming early 2027 among the most sensitive months. In the most recent reports we found (September 2026), no national rationing had been scheduled.

None of that means outages will happen, but if your income depends on being online, it is sensible to:

  • ask whether the building has a backup generator and what it powers (lifts and common areas only, or apartments too);
  • carry a power bank that can charge your laptop, or a small UPS for the router;
  • check EPM and local news before key deadlines.

Checklist: what to ask before booking a monthly apartment for remote work

Ask aboutWhy it matters
A recent in-unit speed test (download and upload)City averages don't tell you about this router
A real desk and an adjustable chairEight hours on a dining chair gets old fast
Ethernet port near the deskMore stable than Wi-Fi for long calls
Noise: street, nightlife, building worksMatters for calls and sleep
Backup power in the buildingRelevant during this season's rationing warnings
Mobile signal inside the unitYour hotspot is your plan B
What's included: utilities, internet, cleaningSo the monthly price has no surprises
Contract length and house rulesMake sure the terms match your stay

Our earlier guide to renting a furnished apartment in Medellín without a fiador covers the contract side in more detail.

Find a furnished place to work from

Browse our furnished rentals in Medellín and ask us about any listing's workspace, internet and what's included before you book.

Own an apartment in Medellín? Remote workers who stay a month or more are a steady market. Our Medellín property management guide explains your options, from Airbnb management in Medellín to long-term property management in Colombia. If you want a team handling dynamic pricing, 24/7 guest support, cleaning and RNT, SIRE and TRA compliance, request a free consultation with Medellín Concierge, specialists in property management in Medellín.

FAQ

Is Medellín good for digital nomads?
For many remote workers, yes: it shares the US Eastern time zone for part of the year and is only an hour off it for the rest, the metro area has fast fixed internet by Colombian standards, and there are coworking spaces and public Wi-Fi. The apartment you choose matters most, so check its speed, desk and backup options before you book.

What internet speed do I need for video calls?
That depends on your video app and how many people share the connection, so check your provider's own requirements. What matters most is a stable connection with good upload speed, so ask for an in-unit speed test and use a cable when you can.

Do I need a visa to work remotely from Medellín?
It depends on your nationality and how long you stay. Read our Colombia digital nomad visa guide and confirm with Cancillería and Migración Colombia before you travel. This is general information, not legal advice.

item.title: How Much Does Airbnb Management Cost in Medellín? Fees, IVA and What's Included (2026)
item.description: How much does Airbnb management cost in Medellín? Fee models, what the % is calculated on, 19% IVA, Airbnb's 15.5% host fee and 8 questions to ask.
item.content:encoded:
Short answer: there is no official or standard fee for managing an Airbnb in Medellín. Many managers charge a percentage of booking revenue, plus Colombia's VAT (IVA) if they are registered for it, and the owner separately pays the platform's commission and the property's own running costs. What you really pay comes down to three things: the percentage, what amount it is calculated on, and which services it covers.

This article shows you how to read a management proposal, what gets added on top of the percentage, and where to find our published fees. If you first want to know what a manager actually does day to day, read Airbnb management in Medellín: what a manager does, and for the big picture, our Medellín property management guide.

General information as of November 2026. This is not legal or tax advice: we are not tax advisors, so please consult a qualified accountant or lawyer about your situation.

How do Airbnb managers in Medellín charge?

Three structures are common. Airbnb's own co-host tools let an owner pay a percentage of each booking, a fixed amount, the cleaning fee, or the cleaning fee plus a percentage, as the Airbnb Help Center on co-host payouts explains. A Bancolombia guide to short-term rentals (in Spanish) likewise notes that a manager can be paid either a percentage or a fixed cost.

Fee modelHow it worksWhat to watch
Percentage of bookingsThe manager earns a % of what is booked each monthYou pay less in a slow month; ask what the % is calculated on
Fixed monthly feeA set amount, booked or notPredictable, but it doesn't move with results
Hybrid or per serviceA % plus charges for cleaning, laundry or setupGet the full list of extra charges in writing

The percentage model lines up incentives: if the property earns nothing, neither does the manager.

A percentage of what? The question that sets your real cost

Two proposals with the same percentage can cost you very different amounts. Before comparing, ask whether the percentage is taken from:

  1. The gross booking value (nightly rate plus cleaning fee).
  2. What Airbnb pays out to the host after its own commission.
  3. Net income after cleaning and other operating costs.

This illustrative example uses a booking subtotal of COP 1,000,000 and a hypothetical 10% rate (not a market rate and not ours; it only shows the effect of the base):

Calculation baseBase amount10% of that base
Gross booking subtotalCOP 1,000,000COP 100,000
After Airbnb's 15.5% host feeCOP 845,000COP 84,500
After also deducting COP 80,000 cleaningCOP 765,000COP 76,500

The first and last rows differ by more than 20%, with the same "10%". When you get a quote, ask the manager to walk you through an example like this one.

Do Colombian property managers charge VAT (IVA)?

As of November 2026, Colombia's general VAT rate is 19%, set by Article 468 of the Tax Statute (as amended by Law 1819 of 2016). In general, when the company providing management or brokerage services is registered for IVA, it adds that tax to its commission, as Gerencie.com explains for real estate agencies (in Spanish).

In practice: if a proposal says "X% + IVA", the effective cost of the commission is that percentage plus 19% of it. If it just says "X%", ask whether IVA is included. How IVA or withholding tax affects you personally depends on your tax situation, especially if you live abroad, so check with an accountant.

Paid separately: Airbnb's own commission

The platform's commission is not the manager's fee. Since 2025, Airbnb has moved most hosts, starting with those connected through property management software, to a single host-only fee. According to Hostfully, that fee is 15.5% of the booking subtotal (nightly rate, cleaning and extra guest or pet fees) in most countries. What do you need before you furnish anything?

Check these before you buy a single sofa. Each one can stop a short-term rental on its own:

How should you furnish an apartment for Airbnb in Medellín?

Furnish for the guest who will actually book, not for yourself. In Medellín that is often a mix of tourists, business travellers and remote workers staying weeks at a time, so durability and function matter more than decoration.

Airbnb's own guide to the amenities guests want names wifi, a kitchen, free parking, a pool and air conditioning among the amenities guests search for most, and advises hosts to list every amenity they offer, because many guests use search filters. item.title: Medellín Rental Yield: How to Calculate Your Real Return Before You Buy (2026)
item.description: How to calculate rental yield in Medellín: gross vs net formula, the costs owners forget (HOA, predial, vacancy) and a worked example. Updated Nov 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Short answer: rental yield in Medellín is your annual rent divided by the total cost of the property (gross yield), and, more usefully, your annual rent minus the year's real costs divided by the same amount (net yield). Global Property Guide puts the average gross rental yield for housing in Colombia at 7.01% in Q1 2026. Net yields are lower once costs are subtracted. But an average is not your apartment: the number that matters is the one built from your own figures.

This guide, current as of November 2026, walks you through the formula, the costs foreign and local owners most often forget, and the questions to ask before you buy or choose between short-term and long-term renting. It is general information, not financial, legal or tax advice. We are not tax advisors, so please consult a qualified professional about your own situation.

What is the difference between gross and net rental yield?

  • Gross yield = (monthly rent × 12) ÷ total property cost × 100. Good for quick comparisons between apartments or neighborhoods.
  • Net yield = (annual income − annual costs) ÷ total investment × 100. This is what you actually keep.

Your total investment is more than the purchase price. Add closing and registration costs, initial repairs and, if you furnish the unit, furniture. Published averages such as Global Property Guide's Colombia figures are gross: they ignore taxes and operating costs.

Which costs should you subtract to get net yield?

These are the costs that weigh most on a Medellín apartment, and where to find the real figure for your unit:

CostWhat it isWhere to get the real number
HOA fee (cuota de administración)Monthly fee charged by the buildingLatest building statement or certificate
Property tax (predial)Municipal tax based on the cadastral valueYour predial bill and the Alcaldía de Medellín tax rules
VacancyMonths without a tenant or nights without bookingsYour history, or a conservative estimate
Maintenance and repairsPaint, appliances, plumbing, wear and tearYour own annual budget
InsuranceProperty policy and, for long-term rentals, rent guarantee insuranceA quote from your insurer
Property managementFees for whoever manages the lease or the AirbnbOur plans or your manager's proposal
Income taxRental income is taxableDIAN and a Colombian accountant or tax advisor

For short-term rentals, also add utilities, internet, cleaning between guests, linen replacement and platform fees. In a long-term lease, whether the owner or the tenant pays the HOA fee depends on the contract, so check it before you run the numbers.

Worked example: how do you calculate it step by step?

The example below is hypothetical, with round numbers to show the method. It is not market data and not a promise of results.

  • Total property cost: COP 400,000,000
  • Monthly rent: COP 2,400,000, so COP 28,800,000 a year
  • Gross yield: 28,800,000 ÷ 400,000,000 = 7.2%

Now subtract the year's costs (also hypothetical): one month of vacancy (COP 2,400,000), an HOA fee of COP 400,000 a month (COP 4,800,000), predial (COP 1,600,000) and maintenance (COP 800,000). Total: COP 9,600,000.

  • Net income: 28,800,000 − 9,600,000 = COP 19,200,000
  • Net yield: 19,200,000 ÷ 400,000,000 = 4.8%, before management fees and income tax.

That is 2.4 points lost to costs that never appear in a listing. It is why you should ask for the real bills before you buy.

Does Airbnb or a long-term rental give a better yield in Medellín?

It depends on the property and, above all, on whether short-term rental is allowed there. Airbnb income is the nightly rate times the nights booked, and both move with the season, the neighborhood and the quality of the listing. Costs are higher too, and the work is daily.

Before you count on a nightly rate, check three things: that the building rules (reglamento de propiedad horizontal) expressly allow tourist rentals, that land-use rules at your address allow them, and that you can hold an active RNT registration. We cover these in Airbnb requirements in Medellín. To compare the two models in depth, read Airbnb vs long-term rental in Medellín.

How much can rent go up each year in Medellín?

As of November 2026, for urban housing, Colombia's Law 820 of 2003 caps the annual rent increase at the previous year's consumer price inflation (IPC). According to Portafolio, citing DANE, 2025 inflation closed at 5.1%, which is the cap for 2026 increases. This matters for your math: in a long-term lease, income grows at most with inflation, so your yield depends heavily on the price you pay. More in our guide to long-term rental management in Medellín.

Quick checklist before you buy to rent

  • Ask for the latest HOA statement and predial bill.
  • Read the building rules: do they allow short-term rentals?
  • Calculate net yield with at least one month of vacancy a year.
  • Add closing costs, registration, repairs and furniture to your total investment.
  • Ask an accountant how rental income is declared in your case.
  • Compare your result with public averages, but never treat them as a guarantee.

You see every income and expense item in the owner portal, with monthly GAAP financial statements, so you can track your real yield month by month. For the full picture, read our Medellín property management guide.

There is no single number. As a reference, Global Property Guide reports an average gross rental yield of 7.01% for Colombia in Q1 2026. What matters is how your net yield compares with your other investment options and your tolerance for risk.

Are the yields quoted online gross or net?
Almost always gross: annual rent divided by price. They leave out HOA fees, predial, vacancy, maintenance and taxes, so your net yield will be lower.

Do foreign owners pay tax on rental income in Colombia?
Rental income from a Colombian property is generally taxable, and how it is taxed depends on your tax residency and situation. Check with DIAN and a qualified Colombian tax advisor; we do not give tax advice.

item.title: Colombia Digital Nomad Visa: How Long Can You Stay in Medellín? (2026)
item.description: How long can you stay in Colombia? Tourist 90+90 day rules, the 2-year Digital Nomad Visa, the 183-day tax rule and what it means for renting in Medellín.
item.content:encoded:
Short answer: most remote workers from visa-exempt countries can stay in Colombia as visitors for up to 90 days, extend once for up to 90 more, and never exceed 180 days in the same calendar year. If you want to live in Medellín longer, Colombia's Digital Nomad Visa (a type V visa) allows a stay of up to two years while you work remotely for employers or clients outside Colombia. Either way, plan your stay length before you sign for a furnished apartment.

This guide is current as of November 2026. It is general information for travellers and remote workers, not legal, immigration or tax advice. Immigration rules and fees change, so always confirm the current requirements with Cancillería and Migración Colombia, or a qualified immigration lawyer, before you travel.

How long can I stay in Colombia as a tourist?

If your passport is from a country that does not need a visa for short stays, Migración Colombia gives you an entry and stay permit (Permiso de Ingreso y Permanencia, PIP) at the airport, usually for up to 90 days (Migración Colombia, PIP).

You can then ask for an extension of up to 90 more days without leaving the country. As of November 2026, under Migración Colombia Resolution 2061 of 2020, your total stay as a visitor cannot exceed 180 days, continuous or not, in the same calendar year (1 January to 31 December). Leaving the country and coming back does not reset that count.

Practical points:

  • Apply for the extension online with Migración Colombia before your current permit expires, and check its website for how far in advance to apply.
  • Only one extension is granted per entry permit, and applying does not guarantee approval.
  • There is a fee, set each year by the authority. Check the current amount on the Migración Colombia website rather than relying on a blog.

Can I work remotely in Colombia without a visa?

As of November 2026, according to Cancillería's Resolution 5477 of 2022, the resolution that regulates Colombian visas, remote workers from visa-exempt countries can enter with an entry permit as long as they receive no payments from Colombian companies and their stay is no longer than 90 days. If you plan to stay longer than that while working, the Digital Nomad Visa is the route designed for you.

What is the Colombia Digital Nomad Visa?

The Digital Nomad Visa is a visitor visa (type V) created by Resolution 5477 of 2022. Colombia's Ministry of Justice summarizes the process in plain Spanish on its LegalApp guide. Based on the resolution, as of November 2026:

  • Who it is for: people who work remotely, by digital means, exclusively for companies or clients outside Colombia, either as employees or as freelancers, and people starting a digital content or information-technology business.
  • How long: up to two years.
  • Passport: you must hold a passport from a country whose nationals do not need a visa for short stays in Colombia.
  • Proof of work: a letter from the foreign employer or client, in Spanish or English, describing the relationship and how you are paid.
  • Income: the resolution ties the minimum income to Colombia's legal monthly minimum wage (SMMLV); the published text asks for at least three minimum wages a month. The 2026 minimum wage is COP 1,750,905 (Decree 159 of 2026), so three works out to COP 5,252,715 a month. Confirm the current figure with Cancillería before you apply.
  • Health insurance: a policy that covers you in Colombia for the length of the visa.
  • Absences: leaving Colombia for 90 calendar days or more ends the visa early.

You apply online through Cancillería's visa portal. Fees are listed by Cancillería and can differ by nationality, so check the official fee table instead of a third-party guide.

Tourist stay or Digital Nomad Visa: which fits your plans?

Visitor entry (PIP)ExtensionDigital Nomad Visa (V)
Typical lengthUp to 90 daysUp to 90 more daysUp to 2 years
Yearly limit180 days per calendar year in totalCounts toward the same 180Not limited by the 180-day visitor rule
Remote work for foreign clientsAllowed for stays up to 90 days with no Colombian payments (Res. 5477)Check with CancilleríaYes, that is its purpose
Where to applyAt the airport, on arrivalMigración Colombia, onlineCancillería, online
Registration after approvalNot requiredNot requiredRegister with Migración Colombia for a foreign ID (cédula de extranjería) if required

If you get a visa valid for more than three months, Migración Colombia requires you to register and obtain a cédula de extranjería, usually within 15 calendar days. Check the exact steps on the Migración Colombia website.

Do digital nomads pay taxes in Colombia?

A visa and tax residency are different things. As of November 2026, under Article 10 of the Tax Statute, a person who stays in Colombia for more than 183 calendar days, continuous or not, within any 365-day period becomes a Colombian tax resident (DIAN). Tax residents are generally taxed on their worldwide income. If you plan to stay that long, speak to a qualified tax professional in Colombia and in your home country. We are not tax advisors.

What does this mean for renting an apartment in Medellín?

Your immigration status shapes your housing plan:

  1. Match the lease to your permit. If you are on a 90-day entry, book for 90 days or less, or make sure the contract lets you leave early if your extension is not approved.
  2. Keep your passport handy. Lodging providers must report foreign guests to Migración Colombia through the SIRE system, so a legitimate host or manager will ask for your passport details.
  3. Think about the address you will use. Visa and registration forms ask for an address in Colombia; a written rental agreement makes that simple.
  4. Choose the neighborhood for your work routine. If you are still deciding, read our guide El Poblado vs Laureles vs Envigado: where to stay in Medellín for a month, and if a landlord asks you for a co-signer, see how to rent a furnished apartment in Medellín without a fiador.

Find a furnished place for your stay

Once you know how long you can stay, browse our monthly rentals in Medellín. Each listing describes the apartment and what is included, and you can ask us about the length of stay that works for your permit or visa before you book.

Own an apartment in Medellín and want to host remote workers? Our Medellín property management guide explains how property management in Medellín works, and our Airbnb management in Medellín and property management in Colombia pages show what we do for owners. Request a free consultation to talk it through.

FAQ

How long can a tourist stay in Colombia in 2026?

Visitors from visa-exempt countries usually get up to 90 days on arrival and can extend once for up to 90 more, with a maximum of 180 days in the same calendar year (Migración Colombia Resolution 2061 of 2020), as of November 2026.

How much income do I need for the Colombia Digital Nomad Visa?

Resolution 5477 of 2022 sets the requirement in multiples of the monthly minimum wage; the published text asks for at least three. With the 2026 minimum wage of COP 1,750,905, that is COP 5,252,715 a month. Confirm the current figure with Cancillería before applying.

Can I rent a furnished apartment in Medellín on a tourist entry?

Yes. Furnished monthly rentals are common for visitors. Keep the rental within your permitted stay, have your passport ready for the SIRE report, and get a written agreement before you pay.
